mainTopic: Pesachim 78b: רבי יוסי's middle view, the משנה on impure meat or fat of the קרבן פסח, and whether eating the פסח is essential (רב, רבי נתן and the רבנן)
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanation of רבי יוסי's middle position between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי יוסי follows רבי יהושע לכתחילה, and he follows רבי אליעזר בדיעבד when the meat was lost or burned. When the meat only became impure, even רבי יהושע accepts the offering after the fact. A new משנה then teaches that for a קרבן פסח, impure meat stops the blood from being sprinkled, but impure fat does not. For other offerings, pure fat alone is enough. רב rules that if the blood was sprinkled anyway, the פסח is accepted, because eating is not essential. After challenges from a פסוק and a ברייתא, the גמרא says רב follows רבי נתן. It proves this from רבי נתן's ruling that even a group with no כזית to eat is exempt from פסח שני, because the blood was already sprinkled. רב chose this reading because the משנה says 'אין זורק' and not 'פסול'. Even רבי נתן requires a person who is fit to eat. The גמרא then tests three ברייתות to see whether each follows רבי נתן or the רבנן. It ends with רבי יוחנן placing the last ברייתא in a case of the ציבור, where the meat is still not eaten because of a rabbinic גזירה.

steps.title: Rejecting the public-offering reading of רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier suggestion that רבי יוסי sided with רבי אליעזר for public offerings. In public offerings, even רבי יהושע already agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you said that with public offerings, even רבי יהושע agrees!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the previous explanation of רבי יוסי's words. That explanation linked רבי אליעזר's view to a קרבן ציבור (an offering brought for the community).
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a קרבן ציבור, impurity is permitted (טומאה הותרה בציבור), so everyone allows sprinkling the blood. If רבי יהושע already agrees in that case, then רבי יוסי could not be 'siding with רבי אליעזר' there, because there is no argument to take a side in. So the reading falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But you (yourself) said; points back to an earlier statement to show a contradiction
The community; refers to communal offerings (קָרְבְּנוֹת צִיבּוּר)
The תנא who requires some meat or fat to remain before the blood may be sprinkled

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of the sugya. 'You said' refers to an earlier rule in the גמרא that impurity is permitted for public offerings. It does not refer to something said here.

phrases.english: But you said
phrases.notes: He's pointing out that this clashes with something already said earlier.

phrases.english: with regard to the public, even Rabbi Yehoshua agrees.
phrases.notes: Because impurity is permitted for communal offerings

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the interpretation of רבי יוסי proposed on the previous amud
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole public-versus-private reading of רבי יוסי's statement
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no מחלוקת about public offerings, so רבי יוסי cannot be choosing רבי אליעזר's side there

steps.title: New reading: after the fact versus from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רבי יוסי. He follows רבי אליעזר בדיעבד and רבי יהושע לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי meant: I see רבי אליעזר's words as correct after the fact, and רבי יהושע's words as correct from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a brand-new explanation of רבי יוסי's statement to replace the one it just rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the split is not between kinds of offerings but between two stages of action. לכתחילה, you should not sprinkle the blood when the meat is gone (רבי יהושע). But if someone already did, the offering counts (רבי אליעזר).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that a new explanation replaces the old one
I see (as correct); רבי יוסי's way of choosing a view
After the fact, once it was already done

phrases.english: Rather: I see (as correct)
the words of Rabbi Eliezer after the fact,
and the words of Rabbi Yehoshua from the outset.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּדִיעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading rejected in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the statement (stage of action instead of type of offering)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי split the views by public versus private offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי split the views by לכתחילה versus בדיעבד

steps.title: But רבי יהושע already agrees after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The new reading is challenged. A ברייתא says that רבי יהושע himself agrees that if the blood was sprinkled, the offering is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the fact, even רבי יהושע agrees! As it teaches: רבי יהושע agrees that if one sprinkled the blood, it is accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new explanation from step 2. It quotes a teaching showing that רבי יהושע has no argument בדיעבד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of problem as in step 1. If רבי יהושע already accepts the offering after the fact, then רבי יוסי is not 'choosing רבי אליעזר' בדיעבד, because both agree. The proof comes from an explicit source (קתני).

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught (in a ברייתא)
It was accepted (the offering is valid)

phrases.aramaic: דִּיעֲבַד — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי מוֹדֶה הוּא,
phrases.english: After the fact, even Rabbi Yehoshua also agrees,
as it teaches: Rabbi Yehoshua agrees
that if one sprinkled, it was accepted!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּיעֲבַד — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי מוֹדֶה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי sides with רבי אליעזר בדיעבד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהושע agrees בדיעבד, so there is no dispute there for רבי יוסי to decide

steps.title: Two different cases: impure meat versus lost or burned meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא and רבי יוסי are talking about different situations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is about impurity; that one is about meat that was lost or burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the step 2 reading by splitting the cases. It gives the short answer here and explains it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways the meat can become unavailable. It can become impure (טמא), or it can be physically gone (lost or burned). רבי יהושע's concession may apply to only one of these.

phrases.english: This is with impurity; that is with lost or burned.
phrases.notes: Classic 'הא בהא' answer that splits the cases

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא of each source in a different scenario)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's concession applies to every case where the meat is unavailable
steps.terutzMaskana: The concession is limited to impurity

steps.title: Spelling out the split: where רבי יהושע agrees and where רבי יוסי sides with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע agrees בדיעבד only when the meat became impure, not when it was lost or burned. רבי יוסי follows רבי אליעזר בדיעבד in the case of lost or burned meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches that רבי יהושע agrees that if one sprinkled it is accepted, that is when the meat became impure, but not when it was lost or burned. When רבי יוסי says 'I see רבי אליעזר's words after the fact,' that is when it was lost or burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its short answer in full. This closes the discussion of רבי יוסי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For impurity, the ציץ (the כהן גדול's headplate) atones, so even רבי יהושע accepts the offering after the fact. For lost or burned meat, nothing makes up for it, so רבי יהושע disagrees even בדיעבד. That is exactly where רבי יוסי sides with רבי אליעזר. So the 'לכתחילה versus בדיעבד' reading survives.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where it became impure
The תנא whose middle-ground statement is being interpreted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's 'הורצה' (it is accepted) after the fact applies only to impure meat. For lost or burned meat, רבי יהושע invalidates the offering even after the fact, and רבי יוסי rules like רבי אליעזר בדיעבד. לכתחילה, רבי יוסי rules like רבי יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'the meat is unavailable' is not one single category. Impurity can be covered by the ציץ's atonement, while physical loss cannot.

phrases.english: When it teaches: Rabbi Yehoshua agrees
that if one sprinkled it is accepted, that is where it became impure,
but with lost or burned, no.
When Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּדִיעֲבַד —
phrases.english: I see the words of Rabbi Eliezer (as correct) after the fact,
that is with lost or burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁאִם זָרַק הוּרְצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the short answer of step 4 and applies it to both sources
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי: לכתחילה like רבי יהושע. בדיעבד, for lost or burned meat, like רבי אליעזר. For impurity, all agree that the offering is accepted after the fact.

steps.title: New משנה: impure meat versus impure fat in the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: For the קרבן פסח: if the meat became impure, the blood is not sprinkled even though the fat is pure. If the fat became impure but the meat is pure, the blood is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the meat became impure and the fat remains, one does not sprinkle the blood. If the fat became impure and the meat remains, one sprinkles the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a rule about the קרבן פסח. It tells us which part of the animal must stay pure for the blood to be sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main purpose of the קרבן פסח is to be eaten. So if the meat cannot be eaten, the offering loses its point, even though the fat could still go on the altar. If only the fat is impure, the eating can still happen, so the blood is sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Sprinkles the blood on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: This חֵלֶב (with a צירה) means the forbidden fats offered on the altar. It is not חָלָב (milk).

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If the meat became impure and the fat remains,
he does not sprinkle the blood.
If the fat became impure and the meat remains,
he sprinkles the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה; unrelated to the רבי יוסי discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a קרבן פסח, pure meat is required for sprinkling; pure fat alone does not suffice

steps.title: Other offerings are different: pure fat is enough
steps.stepSummary: For other קדשים, the blood is sprinkled even if the meat became impure, as long as the fat remains pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with other offerings it is not so. Rather, even though the meat became impure, if the fat remains, one sprinkles the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה contrasts the קרבן פסח with all other offerings and gives a more lenient rule for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other offerings are not mainly about eating. So the fat being fit for the altar is enough of a valid part to justify sprinkling the blood. This shows that the strict rule in step 6 is special to the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated offerings (here: all offerings besides the פסח)

steps.whatToRemember: פסח: the meat must stay pure for the blood to be sprinkled. Other offerings: pure fat alone is enough.

phrases.english: But with (other) consecrated offerings it is not so,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּטְמָא הַבָּשָׂר
phrases.english: rather, even though the meat became impure
and the fat remains,
he sprinkles the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts other offerings with the פסח rule of step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other offerings, pure fat alone allows the blood to be sprinkled

steps.title: רב rules that sprinkling the blood makes the offering accepted
steps.stepSummary: רב גידל quotes רב: if the blood of the פסח was sprinkled, even though the meat became impure, the offering is accepted (הורצה).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב גידל said in the name of רב: If he sprinkled the blood, the offering was accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins with a ruling from רב. Once the blood was sprinkled, the owners have fulfilled their קרבן פסח, even though the meat cannot be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6 and 7 discussed whether we may sprinkle the blood in the first place (לכתחילה) when the meat is impure. רב addresses the after-the-fact (בדיעבד) case: if someone already sprinkled, it still counts. So the owners do not need to bring a פסח שני.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that analyzes the משנה
He sprinkled (the blood on the מזבח)
It was accepted; the owners fulfilled their obligation through the offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets up the whole back-and-forth that follows. Every challenge here is aimed at it.

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
If he sprinkled (the blood), it was accepted.
phrases.notes: This applies even though the meat was impure and cannot be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the לכתחילה rules about sprinkling to a בדיעבד ruling on the case where it was already done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the blood of the פסח has been sprinkled, the offering is accepted (הורצה) even if the meat cannot be eaten.

steps.title: Challenge: the פסח must be eaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a קרבן פסח requires eating (אכילה), and here the meat cannot be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't we need the offering to be eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. How can the פסח count if nobody can eat it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the קרבן פסח is that it is eaten on the night of פסח. If the meat is impure, there is no eating at all. So how can רב say the offering is accepted?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that… (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But don't we require eating!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that sprinkling alone makes the פסח accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח must be eaten. Where eating is impossible, the offering should fail.

steps.title: Answer: eating is not essential
steps.stepSummary: Eating is part of the מצוה, but missing it does not cancel the offering (לא מעכבא).
steps.simpleTranslation: Eating does not hold it back (it is not essential to the offering's validity).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. Eating is not a requirement that blocks the offering from being accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא separates two things. One is what we are supposed to do (eat the פסח). The other is what the offering's acceptance depends on. Here acceptance depends only on sprinkling the blood, so even without eating, the offering counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back; is essential (without it, the act is invalid)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not מעכב' does NOT mean you don't have to eat the פסח. It means that if eating did not happen, the offering is still valid after the fact.

phrases.english: Eating does not prevent (acceptance).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the status of the requirement (a מצוה, not essential)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without eating, the פסח is invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating is required but not essential. Sprinkling alone brings acceptance.

steps.title: Challenge from the verse 'according to every man's eating'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the פסוק 'איש לפי אכלו', which seems to make eating a basic requirement of the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'According to every man's eating'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again, this time with a פסוק. The Torah itself ties the פסח to the people who will eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer said eating is not essential. The פסוק in שמות י״ב:ד׳ counts the פסח according to its eaters, which suggests eating is built into what a פסח is. So the challenge now rests on a verse, not just on logic.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Each man according to his eating' (שמות י״ב:ד׳)

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"According to every man's eating"?!
phrases.notes: From שמות י״ב:ד׳, about counting people for a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 10 using a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that eating is not essential
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah defines the פסח by its eaters, so eating should be essential.

steps.title: Answer: the verse is only for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches the proper way to do the מצוה‎ (למצוה), not a requirement for validity.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for the מצוה (the ideal way to perform it).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with one word. The פסוק tells us how we should do the מצוה, but it does not make the offering invalid if eating can't happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same distinction as in step 10, now applied to the verse. 'איש לפי אכלו' describes the ideal: count the people who will eat. It does not say the קרבן fails without eating.

keyTerms.meaning: For the ideal performance of the מצוה, not as an essential condition

phrases.english: (It is stated) as a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the verse-based challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the verse to the ideal (מצוה), not essential (עיכוב)
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse only describes the proper מצוה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the same verse is essential for registration
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that slaughtering a פסח for people who were not registered (מנויין) makes it invalid. The repeated verse 'איש לפי אכלו תכסו' makes this essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not meant to be essential? But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'According to the number' teaches that the פסח is slaughtered only for its registered members. One might think that if he slaughtered it for people who were not registered, he merely went against the מצוה and it is still valid. So the verse says: 'According to every man's eating you shall count.' The Torah repeated it to make it essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer 'למצוה' by bringing a ברייתא. This step sets up the final punch, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the Torah repeated the counting idea ('במכסת' and then 'תכסו'). When the Torah says something twice, it means it is essential (לעכב). So the very verse step 12 called 'just a מצוה' is treated by the ברייתא as essential, at least for registration.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source against the previous claim)
The count/number (of people registered for the פסח)
Its registered members, who signed up in advance for this פסח
The Torah repeated it to make it essential

phrases.english: And is it not to be essential?
But it was taught (in a ברייתא):
"According to the number",
teaches that the Paschal lamb is not slaughtered
except for its registered members.
One might think: if he slaughtered it for those not registered,
he would be like one who violates a מצוה, but it is valid —
therefore the verse says:
"According to every man's eating you shall count",
the verse repeated it to make it essential.
phrases.notes: When the Torah says something twice, it's telling us the requirement is a must.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 12's claim that the verse is only למצוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that 'איש לפי אכלו' is only for the מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads this very verse as essential (לעכב), because the Torah repeated it.

steps.title: Eaters are linked to registered people, so eating is essential too
steps.stepSummary: The verse links eaters (אוכלין) to registered people (מנויין). Just as registration is essential, eating should be essential, which goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And eaters are compared to registered people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its challenge. Since the same verse joins 'eating' and 'counting', whatever is true for registration is true for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proved that registration (מנויין) is essential. The verse places eaters right next to the count, creating a היקש (a comparison drawn from the verse). So eating should also be essential, which contradicts רב's ruling that sprinkling alone brings acceptance (הורצה).

keyTerms.meaning: They were compared through a היקש (a linkage drawn from the verse)
Those able to eat the offering

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רב moved in three steps: eating is needed, then the verse, then a ברייתא plus a היקש. The final form: eating is linked to registration, and registration is essential, so eating should be essential too. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא itself only talks about registration (מנויין), not eating. The challenge to רב comes from the extra step that links eaters to registration.

phrases.english: And eaters are juxtaposed to registered members.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's rule about registration to eating, completing the challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling (step 8) that the פסח is accepted without eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Registration is essential (from the ברייתא), and eaters are compared to the registered. So eating is essential, and an inedible פסח should not be accepted.

steps.title: רב follows רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenges: רב holds like רבי נתן, who says eating the פסח is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב said his ruling following רבי נתן, who said: eating the פסח offerings does not hold back the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops defending רב's view against the ברייתא. Instead it says רב is following a different תנא, רבי נתן, who agrees that eating is not essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that the ברייתא treats eating like registration (מנויין), which is essential. Instead of reinterpreting that ברייתא, the גמרא says רב sides with רבי נתן, who disagrees with it. Now רב is not standing alone. He has a תנא to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, a signal that the גמרא is changing its approach
A תנא whose opinion רב is said to follow
Does not hold back, meaning it is not essential to validity

steps.confusionAlert: The word אלא here does not mean the earlier answers were wrong about the facts. It means the גמרא now admits the ברייתא disagrees with רב, and it finds רב a different תנא to rely on.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav said it according to Rabbi Natan,
who said: eating the Paschal offerings does not prevent validity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 14 by assigning רב to a dissenting תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a dissenting תנא (רב כתנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's view is contradicted by the ברייתא and has no support.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי נתן, who holds eating is not essential.

steps.title: Which teaching of רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which statement of רבי נתן shows that eating is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי נתן is meant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the actual source. It is setting up a search through רבי נתן's teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying רב follows רבי נתן is only useful if we can find where רבי נתן said this. The גמרא now asks for that source.

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Natan [teaching]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the attribution made in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific ברייתא of רבי נתן that shows eating is not essential.

steps.title: First suggestion: all ישראל can share one פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the source is רבי נתן's teaching that all of ישראל can fulfill their obligation with one פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is this teaching of רבי נתן, as taught in a ברייתא: רבי נתן says, from where do we know that all of ישראל can fulfill their obligation with one פסח? The פסוק says, 'And the whole assembly of the congregation of ישראל shall slaughter it in the afternoon.' Does the whole assembly slaughter it? Only one person slaughters! Rather, it teaches that all of ישראל can fulfill their obligation with one פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible source. One פסח for the whole nation obviously cannot give everyone a כזית to eat, yet they all fulfill their obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the whole congregation slaughters one animal, which is impossible literally. So רבי נתן reads it as teaching that everyone can be counted on one פסח. Since such a huge group could never all eat from it, this seems to show that eating is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: The assembly of the congregation of Israel
If you say, a tentative suggestion

phrases.english: If you say it is this Rabbi Natan, as it was taught,
Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁכׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹצְאִין בְּפֶסַח אֶחָד —
phrases.english: From where do we know that all Israel fulfill their obligation with one Pesach?
The verse says: 'And they shall slaughter it,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל קְהַל עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם״,
phrases.english: the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel, in the afternoon.'
Does the whole assembly slaughter?
Doesn't only one person slaughter!
Rather, it teaches
that all Israel fulfill their obligation with one Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a first answer to the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא that all ישראל can fulfill their obligation with one פסח, even though they cannot all eat from it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי נתן on שמות י״ב:ו׳.

steps.title: Rejected: each person could still eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. In that case each person is potentially able to eat if others withdraw.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, because if these withdraw, it is fit for those, and if those withdraw, it is fit for these!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first source. It says that case may not prove that eating is not essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When all of ישראל register on one פסח, no single person is truly unable to eat. If enough others pull out, any given person could get a כזית. So the offering is still 'fit for eating' for each person, and this does not prove that eating is not needed.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
for if these withdraw, it is fit for those,
and if those withdraw, it is fit for these!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source proposed in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this ברייתא, not the claim that רב follows רבי נתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each individual remains potentially able to eat, so the case does not involve a real lack of eating.

steps.title: Second suggestion: two groups registered on one פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to a different ברייתא of רבי נתן: when a second group registers on a פסח that only has enough for the first group, the first group eats and is exempt, and the second must bring פסח שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is this teaching of רבי נתן, as taught in a ברייתא: If one group registered on it, and then another group registered on it, the first ones, who have a כזית, eat and are exempt from bringing פסח שני. The later ones, who do not have a כזית, do not eat and must bring פסח שני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a better source from רבי נתן. Here there truly is not enough meat for the second group, so this case involves real people who cannot eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike step 18, here the second group really cannot get a כזית, because the first group already has the meat. Even so, the first group's פסח stays valid and they are exempt from פסח שני, although part of the registration was for people who cannot eat. The גמרא will build its proof for רב from this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Registered on it, were counted for the offering
An olive's volume, the minimum amount of eating
The second פסח, a makeup a month later

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a case where some people registered on the פסח truly cannot eat, yet the offering is not ruined. That is exactly the kind of case needed to support רב.

phrases.english: Rather, it is this Rabbi Natan, as it was taught:
One group registered on it,
and then another group registered on it,
the first ones, who have an olive-bulk, eat
and are exempt from performing the second Pesach;

phrases.aramaic: אַחֲרוֹנִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם כַּזַּיִת, אֵין אוֹכְלִין —
phrases.english: the latter ones, who do not have an olive-bulk, do not eat
and are obligated to perform the second Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source from step 17 with a new ברייתא of רבי נתן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא of two groups registered on one פסח, where the first group eats and is exempt and the second brings פסח שני.
steps.raayaObject: Eating is not essential to the validity of the פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי נתן regarding two successive registrations.

steps.title: רבי נתן: both groups are exempt because the blood was sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The punchline of רבי נתן's ברייתא: both the group that ate and the group that did not eat are exempt from פסח שני, because the blood was already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: both these and those are exempt from bringing a פסח שני, because the blood has already been sprinkled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the previous step. This last line is the actual proof that eating is not essential for רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second group never ate from the פסח, yet רבי נתן still exempts them from פסח שני. The reason he gives is the sprinkling of the blood. So for him the blood fulfills the מצוה, and eating does not hold it back.

keyTerms.meaning: The make-up פסח brought a month later
The blood was sprinkled on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
Both these and those are exempt
from performing the second Pesach,
since the blood was already sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ פְּטוּרִין מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי, שֶׁכְּבָר נִזְרַק הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 19 and delivers the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי נתן, eating the פסח is not essential.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's ruling that even the group that did not eat is exempt from פסח שני because the blood was sprinkled.

steps.title: Maybe the second group was exempt only because it could have eaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to deflect the proof: perhaps the second group is exempt because, had the first group withdrawn, the second group would have been fit to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, maybe it is different there. If these people of the first group had withdrawn, the meat would have been fit for the second group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to knock down the proof, using the same kind of reasoning that rejected the first proof in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that the second group was potentially able to eat. So maybe their exemption depends on that potential, not on eating being non-essential. If so, the ברייתא would not prove anything about רב's position.

phrases.english: Still:
perhaps it is different there,
for if these (the first group) withdraw,
it is fit for them (the second group).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 20 with the logic used in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the second ברייתא of רבי נתן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second group's exemption could rest on their potential to eat, not on eating being non-essential.

steps.title: The ברייתא's stated reason shows the blood is what counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if potential eating were the reason, the ברייתא would have said so. It says 'the blood was sprinkled,' so everything depends on the blood and eating is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have taught: 'since the first group was able to withdraw.' Why does it say 'since the blood was already sprinkled'? Learn from this that the matter depends on the blood, and eating does not hold back the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. It looks closely at the exact reason the ברייתא gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא could have given 'they were fit to withdraw' as its reason, but it chose the sprinkling of the blood instead. That choice shows the blood alone fulfills the obligation. So the proof that רבי נתן holds eating is not essential, and that רב follows him, stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it teach (it should have said)
Does not hold back / is not essential

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי נתן, the sprinkling of the blood fulfills the פסח obligation, and eating is not essential. This is the basis for רב's ruling.

phrases.english: If so, let it teach:
since they are fit to withdraw;
why 'since the blood was already sprinkled'?
Learn from this
the matter depends on the blood,
but eating is not essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִיתְנֵי: הוֹאִיל וּרְאוּיִים לִימָּשֵׁךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 21 and confirms the proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the ברייתא's stated reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption might come from the second group's potential to eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא names the blood as the reason, so eating is not essential for רבי נתן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי נתן, the matter depends on the blood and eating is not essential.

steps.title: Why did רב read the משנה like רבי נתן and not the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what forced רב to read the משנה as a לכתחילה rule following רבי נתן. It could have followed the רבנן, and then even בדיעבד the offering would not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: What pushed רב to explain our משנה as speaking only לכתחילה, following רבי נתן? Let him explain it like the רבנן, and say that even after the fact it does not work!
steps.whatsHappening: With רבי נתן's view now established, the גמרא challenges רב's choice to explain the משנה according to him rather than the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we try to explain a משנה according to the רבנן. Under the רבנן, the משנה's rule would be absolute, meaning invalid even בדיעבד. So why did רב choose the minority opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: That he establishes it (explains it as)

phrases.english: What compelled Rav
to establish the mishna as ab initio,
and according to Rabbi Natan?
Let him establish it like the Rabbis,
and even after the fact, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the established view of רבי נתן and questions why רב needed it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's reading of the משנה as a לכתחילה rule following רבי נתן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simpler reading according to the majority רבנן is available, so why adopt the minority view?

steps.title: The משנה's wording 'he should not sprinkle' forced רב's reading
steps.stepSummary: רב was bothered by the משנה's wording. It says 'one does not sprinkle the blood' rather than 'it is פסול,' which implies a לכתחילה rule only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב had a difficulty with the משנה: why does it say 'one does not sprinkle the blood'? It should say 'it is invalid.' Rather, learn from this that 'one does not sprinkle' means לכתחילה, but after the fact it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 23 by pointing to the exact language of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant the offering is invalid even בדיעבד, it would have used the word 'פסול.' Instead, it gives an instruction not to sprinkle, which is a לכתחילה phrasing. That wording only fits רבי נתן, who allows it בדיעבד.

phrases.english: Rav had difficulty with the mishna:
why does it teach 'one does not sprinkle the blood'?
Let it teach 'invalid.'
Rather, learn from this:
'one does not sprinkle' — ab initio,
but after the fact it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could follow the רבנן and invalidate the offering even בדיעבד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase 'אין זורק' rather than 'פסול' shows a לכתחילה rule, which fits only רבי נתן.
steps.whatToRemember: רב followed רבי נתן because the משנה says 'אין זורק,' which implies the offering works בדיעבד.

steps.title: What does איש לפי אכלו teach according to רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: If eating is not essential for רבי נתן, the גמרא asks why the תורה needs the phrase 'איש לפי אכלו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי נתן, why do I need the verse 'each person according to his eating'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נתן's view by pointing to a verse that seems to stress eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links registering for the פסח to a person's eating. If eating is not essential, this verse seems to have no purpose. The challenge is that the verse would be unnecessary for רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: Each person according to his eating (שמות יב:ד)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Natan,
why do I need 'each man according to his eating'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי נָתָן, אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 22 from a verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן's view that eating is not essential.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse ties the פסח to eating, so it would be pointless if eating were not essential.

steps.title: The verse requires a person who is fit to eat
steps.stepSummary: The verse teaches that the person must be capable of eating, even if actual eating is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we need a person who is fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 25 by giving the verse a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, the verse is not about actually eating. It is about who may be counted for the פסח: someone physically able to eat. A person who cannot eat at all, such as someone very sick, does not fulfill the obligation, even though a fit person who ends up not eating does.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נתן, actual eating is not essential, but the person must be capable of eating.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas: 'eating is not essential' and 'the person must be fit to eat' do not contradict each other. One is about the act; the other is about who qualifies.

phrases.english: Because we require a person
who is fit for eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seems to require actual eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse requires only that the person be fit to eat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: someone unable to eat at all cannot be counted for the פסח, even according to the view that eating is not essential.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about sprinkling the blood for non-eaters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It says that if the פסח was slaughtered for its eaters but the blood was sprinkled for non-eaters, the פסח is valid. The גמרא suggests this follows only רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? It says: if they slaughtered the פסח for the people who will eat it, but sprinkled its blood for people who cannot eat it, the פסח is valid and a person fulfills his obligation with it. Whose view is this? Shall we say it is רבי נתן and not the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and tries to figure out which side of the dispute it matches. It suggests it fits only רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the sprinkling, the blood was meant for people who cannot eat. If eating is essential, as the רבנן hold, that should be a problem. רבי נתן says eating is not essential, so for him the פסח is clearly fine. That is why the ברייתא looks like it follows רבי נתן alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught? (asking which תנא is behind a teaching)
Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא is testing)
For its eaters, meaning the people registered to eat it

steps.confusionAlert: נֵימָא is only a suggestion, not a conclusion. The גמרא is about to push back on it.

phrases.english: Who taught this
that the Rabbis taught in a baraita:
If they slaughtered it for its eaters
and sprinkled its blood not for its eaters
the Pesach itself is valid,
and a person fulfills his obligation with it.
According to whom?
Shall we say it is Rabbi Natan,
and not the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the established dispute between רבי נתן and the רבנן to test a new ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does this ברייתא follow only רבי נתן, so that the רבנן would disagree with it?

steps.title: Even the רבנן agree, because intent about eaters does not matter at sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Wrong intent about the eaters only disqualifies at שחיטה, not at זריקה. So the רבנן can also hold this ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן. Intent about the eaters does not count during the sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and shows that the ברייתא can match the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not really about whether eating is essential. It is about intent regarding the eaters. That kind of intent only matters at the slaughter. At the slaughter, the intent here was correct, so the פסח is valid according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (shows the other side can also accept the source)
Intent regarding who will eat the offering
Sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Even if you say it is the Rabbis,
intent regarding eaters does not apply at the sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא fits only רבי נתן
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attempt to link the ברייתא only to רבי נתן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about intent, which only matters at שחיטה. It is not about whether eating is essential.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about a person who was sick at slaughter or at sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says that a person who is sick at either the שחיטה or the זריקה cannot have the פסח brought for him. He must be healthy for the whole time. The גמרא suggests this follows only the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? It says: if a person was sick at the time of slaughter and healthy at the time of sprinkling, or healthy at slaughter and sick at sprinkling, we do not slaughter or sprinkle for him. He must be healthy from the slaughter until the sprinkling. Whose view is this? Shall we say it is the רבנן and not רבי נתן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא and suggests it fits only the רבנן, who hold that eating is essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick person cannot eat meat. Requiring him to be able to eat during the whole process sounds like eating matters. If eating is not essential, as רבי נתן says, why should his sickness stop the offering? So the ברייתא seems to follow only the רבנן.

phrases.english: Who taught this
that the Rabbis taught:
One who was sick at the time of slaughter
and healthy at the time of sprinkling,
or healthy at the time of slaughter
and sick at the time of sprinkling.
We do not slaughter or sprinkle for him,
until he is healthy
from the time of slaughter until the time of sprinkling.
According to whom?
Shall we say it is the Rabbis,
and not Rabbi Natan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same test as step 27, but this time the ברייתא seems to favor the other side
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does this ברייתא follow only the רבנן, so that רבי נתן would disagree with it?

steps.title: Even רבי נתן requires a person who is able to eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Even רבי נתן requires the person to be fit to eat, even though actual eating is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי נתן. We need a person who is fit to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי נתן can also accept this ברייתא, using the idea from step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן says the actual eating is not essential. He still agrees that the person must be capable of eating, which is what איש לפי אכלו teaches. A sick person is not capable of eating, so even רבי נתן would not bring the offering for him.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי נתן there are two separate ideas. Actual eating is not essential, but being able to eat is required. Both ברייתות so far fit both sides.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "eating is not essential" with "the person's ability to eat does not matter." רבי נתן holds the first idea, not the second.

phrases.english: Even if you say it is Rabbi Natan,
we require a person who is fit for eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 29 by applying the rule from step 26
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attempt to link the ברייתא only to the רבנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about the person's ability to eat, which רבי נתן also requires. It is not about whether actual eating is essential.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about owners who became impure after slaughter?
steps.stepSummary: A third ברייתא says that if the owners became impure after a pure שחיטה, the blood is still sprinkled but the meat is not eaten. The גמרא asks whose view this is. The answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught this ברייתא? It says: if one slaughtered the פסח in purity, and afterward the owners became impure, the blood is sprinkled in purity, but the meat is not eaten in impurity. Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא and asks whose view it follows. This sets up the next discussion, so the answer has not come yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blood is sprinkled even though the owners cannot eat the meat because of טומאה. At first glance, this fits רבי נתן, who says eating is not essential. The גמרא will now check whether the רבנן can also accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Owners (the people the קרבן is brought for)

phrases.english: Who taught this
that the Rabbis taught:
If one slaughtered it in purity,
and afterward the owners became impure
the blood should be sprinkled in purity,
and the meat should not be eaten in impurity.
According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third ברייתא in the same series of attribution tests
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the dispute does this ברייתא follow, given that the blood is sprinkled even though the owners cannot eat?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the ברייתא follows only רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers the question from step 31. The ברייתא reflects a מחלוקת, and it follows רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: This law is taught as part of a dispute, and it follows רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now answers the question of whose view the ברייתא follows. רבי אלעזר says it matches only רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the owners are טמא, so nobody can eat the meat, yet the blood is still sprinkled. That only makes sense for רבי נתן, who says eating is not essential to the פסח. The רבנן say eating is essential, so in their view there would be no point in sprinkling the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught as part of a dispute, so it is not everyone's view
The תנא who holds that eating the פסח is not essential

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: Some versions have אליעזר in round brackets, but read it as רבי אלעזר, the אמורא who was רבי יוחנן's student; that's why רבי יוחנן answers next. It's not the תנא רבי אליעזר who argued with רבי יהושע at the start of the amud.

phrases.english: It is taught as a matter of dispute,
and it follows Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question 'whose view is this?' from step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion does the ברייתא of the owners becoming טמא follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only רבי נתן's, since the blood is sprinkled even though no one can eat the meat.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even the רבנן agree in a case of the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא can follow the רבנן too. It is talking about the ציבור, who may bring the פסח even in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it follows the רבנן. What case are we dealing with here? The ציבור, which brings the פסח even in a state of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי אלעזר. He explains the ברייתא so that even the רבנן can accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of the ציבור is טמא, the קרבן פסח is brought anyway, because the rule of טומאה is pushed aside for the community. So sprinkling the blood for impure owners is fine even according to the רבנן. The ברייתא no longer proves anything about the dispute between רבי נתן and the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the Rabbis
What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows the case)
The community, meaning a majority of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן is saying the רבנן changed their view that eating is essential. He is only placing the ברייתא in a special case, the ציבור, where טומאה does not stop the פסח.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it follows the Rabbis.
With what case are we dealing here?
With the community,
who perform it even in a state of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן הִיא הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing answer to רבי אלעזר's, so the ברייתא can fit both sides.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא (limiting the ברייתא to a specific case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא must follow רבי נתן, since the blood is sprinkled when no one can eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the ציבור, where the פסח is brought even in טומאה, so the רבנן agree too.

steps.title: If it is the community, why can't they eat the meat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. If the ציבור may bring the פסח in טומאה, they should also be allowed to eat it. So why does the ברייתא say the meat is not eaten?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about the community, why is the meat not eaten in impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's case. It points out that the ברייתא's ruling, that the meat is not eaten, does not fit a case of the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ציבור brings the פסח in טומאה, they also eat it in טומאה. Yet the ברייתא says the meat is not eaten. That detail seems to show the case is not about the ציבור after all.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is about the community

phrases.english: If it is about the community,
why is the meat not eaten in impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּצִיבּוּר אַמַּאי אֵין הַבָּשָׂר נֶאֱכָל בְּטוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's case of the ציבור from step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the ברייתא deals with the ציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ציבור that may offer in טומאה may also eat in טומאה, but the ברייתא forbids eating the meat.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree to prevent confusion between cases
steps.stepSummary: The meat is forbidden because of a גזירה. Otherwise people might eat when they became טמא after the זריקה, wrongly comparing it to an earlier year.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, lest the owners become impure after the sprinkling and say: 'Last year, didn't we become impure and eat? Now too, let us eat.' They would not realize that last year, when the blood was sprinkled, the owners were already impure, while now the owners were pure at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ban on eating is a rabbinic גזירה meant to stop people from mixing up two similar-looking cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different cases. If the owners were טמא at the time of the זריקה, the פסח was offered in טומאה and may be eaten. If they were טהור at the זריקה and became טמא only afterward, they may not eat. Since people could easily confuse these, the חכמים forbade eating even in the first case, and so רבי יוחנן's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
After the sprinkling of the blood

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר says the ברייתא follows only רבי נתן. רבי יוחנן says even the רבנן hold it, in a case of the ציבור. In that case the meat is still not eaten, because of a גזירה: what counts is whether the owners were טמא at the moment of the זריקה, and people would confuse impurity before the זריקה with impurity after it.
steps.confusionAlert: The key moment is the זריקה, not the eating. Being טמא when the blood is sprinkled is different from becoming טמא afterward, even though the owners are equally טמא at mealtime in both cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves רבי יוחנן's reading. It shows the ברייתא is not a proof for רבי נתן against the רבנן.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest the owners become impure
after the sprinkling,
and they will say: Last year, didn't we become impure and eat?
Now too, let us eat.
But they do not know that last year,
when the blood was sprinkled,
the owners were impure,
while now the owners were pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִטָּמְאוּ הַבְּעָלִים לְאַחַר זְרִיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34 and defends רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a case of the ציבור the meat should be eaten even in טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law it could be eaten, but the חכמים forbade it so people would not eat when they became טמא after the זריקה.
